title: Report: Ford Mustang Shelby GT350 Replacement Will Be Based on the Dark Horse SC

body_markdown:
Ford has chosen not to enlist the help of Shelby to develop the high-power variants of[the current-gen Mustang](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2024-ford-mustang-gt-review-the-v-8-standard-bearer-gets-even-better/) . The new[Dark Horse SC](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2026-mustang-dark-horse-sc-first-drive-power-chord/) trim replaces[the Mustang Shelby GT500](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/first-2020-shelby-gt500-is-one-mean-green-machine/) , and a recent report suggests an additional Dark Horse variant due out in the coming months will succeed[the Ford Mustang Shelby GT350](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/2019-mustang-shelby-gt350-turns-up-the-wick-fwith-new-tires-and-aero/) . It will feature a naturally-aspirated V-8 and a six-speed stick.


Citing anonymous insiders, website *[Ford Authority](https://fordauthority.com/2026/11/mustang-shelby-gt350-successor-coming-based-around-dark-horse-sc-exclusive/)* wrote that the next GT350 (which[could be called Dark Horse Boss](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/ford-mustang-dark-horse-boss-trademark/) ) will pick up where its predecessor left off by putting a big focus on track-ready performance. Power will reportedly come from a naturally aspirated V-8 that will be linked to a Tremec six-speed manual transmission, though an automatic could be available as an option.


Ford will need to position the model carefully to ensure it doesn’t overlap with[the Dark Horse](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2024-ford-mustang-dark-horse-review-proven-ingredients-new-recipe/) , which is rated at 500 horsepower, and the Dark Horse SC, which develops 795 horsepower. It’s not terribly far-fetched to expect an output of between 600 and 650 horsepower, though that’s pure speculation. For context,[the last-gen GT350](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/hagerty-insider/modern-gt350-becoming-collectible/) ‘s 5.2-liter Voodoo V-8 was rated at 526 horsepower.

Cooling system upgrades, bigger brakes, and a track-focused suspension would further differentiate the GT350’s successor from the Dark Horse. *Ford Authority* added that the brakes and the suspension could come directly from the Dark Horse SC. Its sources said that the model will only be available as a coupe, which makes sense: Ford didn’t offer the last GT350 as a convertible, either.


The report adds that this car will go on sale next year as a 2027 model, which suggests that it will make its debut in the first half of the year. It would likely land as a 2028 model if it broke cover in, say, December 2027. Pricing could start in the vicinity of $80,000 to split the difference between the Dark Horse ($65,080) and the Dark Horse SC ($106,585).


Keep in mind that nothing is official yet. Ford hasn’t commented on the report, and it hasn’t announced what it will replace the Mustang Shelby GT350 with. What’s seemingly certain is that the model’s successor won’t wear Shelby branding: Ford ended its licensing agreement with Shelby, reportedly because the company ended up paying millions in licensing fees to use the name.


The GT350 nameplate isn’t getting consigned to the automotive attic—you’ll just have to head to Shelby itself rather than Ford to buy one. In early 2025, Shelby unveiled[a current-gen Mustang-based GT350](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/shelby-american-mines-its-history-to-resurrect-the-gt350/) with either a naturally aspirated or a supercharged V-8, a lowered suspension, and heritage-laced Shelby-specific styling.
